title: Travis Kalanick resigns as Uber CEO
trigger: A viral video of Kalanick arguing with an Uber driver, combined with sexual harassment allegations from a former employee and a Waymo trade secrets lawsuit, led major investors led by Benchmark Capital to demand his resignation.

timeline.event: Former engineer Susan Fowler publishes blog post detailing sexual harassment at Uber
Viral video surfaces showing Kalanick arguing with an Uber driver over fares
Waymo sues Uber over alleged trade secrets theft involving former Google engineer Anthony Levandowski
Emil Michael and two other executives leave Uber
Benchmark Capital and other major investors send letter to Kalanick demanding he take a leave of absence and step down as CEO
Kalanick resigns as CEO of Uber, remains on board

outcome.summary: Kalanick resigned as CEO under investor pressure but remained on Uber's board. Dara Khosrowshahi was appointed as successor CEO in August 2017. Uber settled the Waymo trade secrets lawsuit in February 2018 for approximately $245 million in equity. The sexual harassment investigation led to the departure of over 20 employees.

claims.text: Susan Fowler's blog post detailed systemic sexual harassment and retaliation at Uber
The viral video showed Kalanick berating an Uber driver about fare reductions
Waymo's lawsuit alleged that Uber stole self-driving car trade secrets through former Google engineer Anthony Levandowski
Emil Michael and two other executives left Uber amid the leadership crisis
Benchmark Capital led investor pressure demanding Kalanick take a leave of absence and step down as CEO
Kalanick resigned as CEO on June 21, 2017 but remained on Uber's board
